summary: A clip can be warmed, cooled, brightened, made punchier or more colourful from Add Effect > Color Grade: five sliders (Temperature, Tint, Exposure, Contrast, Saturation), each keyable, the same in playback, scrubbing and the exported movie.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording (Help > Open Sample Recording or the Welcome window).

try.do: Click the clip on the timeline to pick it.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so picked controls read grey rather than blue.

try.do: Press the + on the Effects header and choose Color Grade: the clip turns a little warmer and a Color Grade row appears, reading adjust.
Drag Temperature all the way right: the recording turns orange.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so picked controls read grey rather than blue.

try.do: Drag Temperature to the middle, type 0 in Contrast and 100 in Saturation: the clip is exactly as recorded.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so picked controls read grey rather than blue.

try.do: At 0:00 click the diamond in front of Temperature, move to 0:01 and drag Temperature right: a second key, and a Temperature lane under the clip.
try.shotNote: This picture shows the window behind another app, so picked controls read grey rather than blue.

try.do: Press Space: the clip warms over its first second, and File > Export writes it the same.

evaluate: Is the warm look it arrives with right, or should it arrive changing nothing (card: Is this the Color Grade you want on a clip?)
Is Temperature 100 too orange for a screen recording, or about what you would reach for?
Are the five sliders the ones you reach for first, in the order you expect from Premiere's Lumetri?
Does the small diamond in front of each name read as the way to animate that value?
See the contact sheet (2026-10-17-color-grade-contact-sheet.png) and reel (2026-10-17-color-grade-reel.gif): untouched, as it arrives, at the warm end, and put back.
rough: The mock's row reads Warm grade with a drag grip; ours reads Color Grade (the menu item's own name) and sits fixed at the top of Effects with no grip, like Blur, since its place changes nothing. Settled by card a-clip-can-be-colour-graded-from-add-effect-is-this-the-color-grade-you-want.
The mock's menu row says Color grade; ours says Color Grade (UX-PATTERNS §7, menu rows are Title Case).

The grade's sliders are shorter than Appearance's because Effects settings are indented; the key diamond sits inside the name's column, as the mock's property rows put it, so it costs the track nothing, and Temperature's name is set a touch tighter to fit beside it.
Saturation is now offered in Animate a property on every picture at 100%, as the mock's catalogue lists it, so the Animating count reads one more than before on every clip.
The grade as its own track with a blend mode and a matte, and a saved look in the Library, from video-compositing.html, are not in this: task a-colour-grade-can-be-its-own-track-over-the-cli.
